Charles, Prince of Viana.fact: Aspiring to marry Isabella of Castile, he was then thrown into prison by his father, and the Catalans rose in his favor.

Charles, Prince of Viana.subject: Women & Society
Charles, Prince of Viana.question: This insurrection soon became general and _____ was obliged to yield
Charles, Prince of Viana.fact: In 1458 Alfonso died and John became king of Aragon, while Charles was offered the crowns of Naples and Sicily. This insurrection soon became general and John was obliged to yield.

Charles, Prince of Viana.fact: He released his son, and recognized him as perpetual governor of Catalonia, and heir to the kingdom.

Charles, Prince of Viana.question: He translated Aristotle's Ethics into Aragonese, a work first published at Zaragoza in _____, and wrote a chronicle of the kings of Navarre, Cronica de los reyes de Navarra
Charles, Prince of Viana.fact: He translated Aristotle's Ethics into Aragonese, a work first published at Zaragoza in 1509, and wrote a chronicle of the kings of Navarre, Cronica de los reyes de Navarra.

Charles, Prince of Viana.subject: Women & Society
Charles, Prince of Viana.question: Agnes died, childless, on 6 April 1448, eight years after her marriage to _____, aged only about twenty-six
Charles, Prince of Viana.fact: Charles, Prince of Viana (Basque: Karlos IV.a) (29 May 1421 – 23 September 1461), sometimes called Charles IV of Navarre, was the eldest son of King John II of Aragon and Queen Blanche I of Navarre. Both his grandfather Charles and his mother, who ruled over Navarre from 1425 to 1441, had bequeathed this kingdom to Charles, whose right had also been recognized by the Cortes; but when Blanche died in 1441 her husband John seized the kingdom to the exclusion of his son.

Charles, Prince of Viana.subject: Women & Society
Charles, Prince of Viana.question: In 1458 _____ died and John became king of Aragon, while Charles was offered the crowns of Naples and Sicily
Charles, Prince of Viana.fact: Released upon promising not to take the kingly title until after his father's death, the prince, again unsuccessful in an appeal to arms, took refuge in Naples with King Alfonso V of Aragon. In 1458 Alfonso died and John became king of Aragon, while Charles was offered the crowns of Naples and Sicily.

Charles, Prince of Viana.subject: Women & Society
Charles, Prince of Viana.question: He declined these proposals, and having been reconciled with his father, returned to _____ in 1459
Charles, Prince of Viana.fact: When Joanna began to interfere in the internal affairs of Navarre, a civil war broke out, and in 1452 Charles, although aided by King John II of Castile, was defeated and taken prisoner. He declined these proposals, and having been reconciled with his father, returned to Navarre in 1459.

Chatti.fact: The Chatti were a Roman era Germanic people that lived in a region approximately corresponding to the modern German federal state of Hesse. In this context they were among the defeated opponents of Drusus the Elder, during his Germanic campaigns from 12 BC until his death in 9 BC.

Chatti.fact: A new regional "Rhine-Weser" material culture developed during the first century AD, which was influenced by both the Romans, and the Elbe Germanic peoples including the Suebi who lived to their east, near the Elbe river. This period of change is believed to have also involved a switch from Celtic to Germanic languages, which also originated near the Elbe.

Chatti.fact: He reported them to be mobile and militarized, and creating major disruptions as far away as present day France and Switzerland, even forcing populations to move from their homelands.

Chatti.fact: It is speculated that this conflict was influenced by the arrival of both the Romans and the Suebi in their region.

The Batavi and Cananefates were known for their soldiers, who became important within the Roman military.

While linguists typically seek to explain names from this period and region as either Celtic or Germanic, the significant spelling variations in the Chatti name are seen by scholars as showing patterns known from both language families in this period.

Chatti.subject: Women & Society

Chatti.fact: While linguists typically seek to explain names from this period and region as either Celtic or Germanic, the significant spelling variations in the Chatti name are seen by scholars as showing patterns known from both language families in this period. It has therefore been argued that the name as it came to Roman era authors was originally Celtic, although most of the Chatti had recently become Germanic speakers when they came into contact with Rome.

The name could have evolved further in two different ways, among Celtic and Germanic speakers.

Chatti.fact: Germanic speakers also sometimes appear to have applied this soundchange to Celtic loanwords, for example in the case of the Celtic Volcae, whose name became Walha in Germanic.

Chatti.fact: This may represent a θ-sound as in English "th", or an affricate "ts".

Many Celtic or Gaulish peoples of this time had names ending in -casses/-cassi, such as the Bodiocasses, Durocasses, Veliocasses, Viducasses, Sucasses, Tricasses.

Chatti.fact: Many Celtic or Gaulish peoples of this time had names ending in -casses/-cassi, such as the Bodiocasses, Durocasses, Veliocasses, Viducasses, Sucasses, Tricasses. In the 21st century, the broader proposal that the Chatti were Germanised Celts has been the subject of more detailed proposals by Wagner and Toorians to explain how the medieval and modern name of Hesse apparently evolved from an originally Celtic name of the Chatti.

Chatti.subject: Women & Society
Chatti.question: However, many other proposals including derivations from _____ also exist, beginning with Jakob Grimm who proposed that the name is related to English "hat"
Chatti.fact: However, many other proposals including derivations from Germanic also exist, beginning with Jakob Grimm who proposed that the name is related to English "hat".

Chatti.subject: Women & Society

Chatti.fact: Tacitus also described the Canninefates, who lived in the delta, sharing the same large island with the Batavi, as being the same as the Batavi in origin, language, and valour, but smaller in numbers.

Chatti.subject: Women & Society
Chatti.question: The second element in the name is common among _____ peoples, especially in this region, such as Chasuarii "dwellers on the river Hase", Ampsivarii "dwellers on the river Ems", and the Angrivarii
Chatti.fact: The second element in the name is common among Germanic peoples, especially in this region, such as Chasuarii "dwellers on the river Hase", Ampsivarii "dwellers on the river Ems", and the Angrivarii.

Chatti.subject: Women & Society
Chatti.question: The Chattuarii lived to the east of the Rhine delta, outside the Roman empire, but close to the Batavi and _____
Chatti.fact: The Chattuarii lived to the east of the Rhine delta, outside the Roman empire, but close to the Batavi and Canninefates.

Chatti.subject: Women & Society
Chatti.question: They therefore propose that these were _____ speaking newcomers to the region, probably Suebi, and without the same Celtic heritage
Chatti.fact: Wagner and Rübekeil note that this name has a Germanic ending, and is always spelled with "-tt-", not "-tth-", unlike the name of the Chatti. They therefore propose that these were Germanic speaking newcomers to the region, probably Suebi, and without the same Celtic heritage.

Chatti.subject: Women & Society
Chatti.question: He noted how Dio Cassius described how the Chatti, like their offshoots the Batavi, Cananefates and _____, were assigned land by the Romans shortly before they first appear in the historical records
Chatti.fact: He noted how Dio Cassius described how the Chatti, like their offshoots the Batavi, Cananefates and Mattiaci, were assigned land by the Romans shortly before they first appear in the historical records. Tacitus did not explicitly describe the Mattiaci as an offshoot of the Chatti, but he emphasized their similarity with the Batavi not only in terms of their special military alliance with Rome, but also in other ways (cetera similes Batavi).

Chatti.subject: Women & Society

Chatti.fact: The first surviving Roman reports of the region were made during the Gallic Wars of Julius Caesar in 58-52 BC, do not mention the Chatti, but they do mention the entry of Suebi into the area.

Chatti.subject: Women & Society

Chatti.fact: From the second half of the 1st century AD archaeologists classify the Chatti as Rhine-Weser Germanic peoples, implying a connection to Germanic languages.

Chatti.subject: Women & Society
Chatti.question: On the eastern side of the Rhine lived the _____ to the north and the Ubii to the south
Chatti.fact: On the eastern side of the Rhine lived the Sugambri to the north and the Ubii to the south.

Chatti.subject: Women & Society
Chatti.question: However, he reported that to their east, near the north of what is now Hesse, the _____ had established themselves
Chatti.fact: However, he reported that to their east, near the north of what is now Hesse, the Germanic Suebi had set up themselves.

Chatti.subject: Women & Society
Chatti.question: These were a mobile and militarized people, threatening the area from a position east of the _____
Chatti.fact: On the eastern side of the Rhine lived the Sugambri to the north and the Ubii to the south. These were a mobile and militarized people, threatening the area from a position east of the Ubii.

Chatti.subject: Women & Society
Chatti.question: A further indication of their position is given by his description of the _____ and Usipetes as two Germanic peoples who had been forced to leave their homeland under pressure from the Suebi
Chatti.fact: A further indication of their position is given by his description of the Tencteri and Usipetes as two Germanic peoples who had been forced to leave their homeland under pressure from the Suebi.

Chatti.subject: Women & Society
Chatti.question: Their homeland was apparently east of the Rhine delta, in the vicinity of the _____, with whom they were able to seek refuge when attacked by Caesar
Chatti.fact: Their homeland was apparently east of the Rhine delta, in the vicinity of the Sugambri, with whom they were able to seek refuge when attacked by Caesar. The Sugambri still lived between the Chatti and the Rhine, and their area of control now stretched further south, encompassing the region which the Rome-allied Ubii had left vacant after moving, like the Batavi and Canninefates, to the western side of the Rhine, under Roman control.

Chatti.subject: Women & Society
Chatti.question: East of the Suebi was a dense forest, the _____ (possibly the Harz), and then the Cherusci
Chatti.fact: East of the Suebi was a dense forest, the Silva Bacenis (possibly the Harz), and then the Cherusci.

Chatti.subject: Women & Society
Chatti.question: The Sugambri and the Suebi were defeated by the _____ in 9 BC, and ceased to exist in this region
Chatti.fact: The Sugambri and the Suebi were defeated by the Drusus in 9 BC, and ceased to exist in this region.

Chatti.subject: Women & Society
Chatti.question: Many were subsequently moved west of the Rhine, and many Suebi apparently joined the _____ in their move to Bohemia
Chatti.fact: Many were subsequently moved west of the Rhine, and many Suebi apparently joined the Marcomanni in their move to Bohemia.

Chatti.subject: Women & Society
Chatti.question: The Bructeri lands which lay north of the old _____ lands (and now north of the Tencteri) were according to Tacitus currently under the occupation of the Chamavi and Angrivarii
Chatti.fact: The Sugambri and the Suebi were defeated by the Drusus in 9 BC, and ceased to exist in this region. At the end of the 1st century AD, Tacitus described the situation which had developed in the preceding generations of Roman hegemony: To their west, the Sugambri state near the Rhine had been destroyed by the Romans, and Tacitus reported that the Tencteri and Usipetes had now moved into the area between the Rhine and the Chatti.

Chatti.subject: Women & Society
Chatti.question: Destroyed by _____, its location is not known today, but generally it is assumed to be in the wider neighbourhood of Fritzlar
Chatti.fact: Destroyed by Germanicus, its location is not known today, but generally it is assumed to be in the wider neighbourhood of Fritzlar.

Chatti.subject: Women & Society
Chatti.question: In 9 BC, in this same campaign Drusus also defeated the _____, and an alliance of the Sugambri, Cherusci and Suevi
Chatti.fact: In 9 BC, in this same campaign Drusus also defeated the Marcomanni, and an alliance of the Sugambri, Cherusci and Suevi. These victories led to the disappearance of the Marcomanni, Sugambri, and Suebi from the region of the Chatti, while the Tencteri, Usipetes and Cherusci remained, though now pacified, and under Roman hegemony.

Chatti.subject: Women & Society

Chatti.fact: In this victory the Romans were able to release Romans who had been captured at the Varus disaster in the Teutoburg Forest and been slaves for 40 years.

Chatti.subject: Women & Society
Chatti.question: They were defeated by the governor of _____
Chatti.fact: They were allies of Lucius Antonius Saturninus the governor of Germania Superior in his revolt of 89 AD, but drifting ice on the Rhine prevented them, and they were subsequently attacked by the loyal governor of Germania Inferior. The Chatti appear again during the build up to the Marcomannic Wars, attacking southwards towards Germania superior and Raetia in what is now southern Germany, in 162.

Chatti.subject: Women & Society

Chatti.fact: A few years later, once the bigger battles were being fought, they were repulsed together with the Hermunduri from the Rhine by Didius Julianus in 175.

Fira (typeface).fact: Fira Sans is a humanist sans-serif typeface designed by Erik Spiekermann, Ralph du Carrois, Anja Meiners, Botio Nikoltchev of Carrois Type Design, and Patryk Adamczyk of Mozilla Corporation. The typeface was originally commissioned by Telefónica and Mozilla Corporation as part of the joint effort during the development of Firefox OS.
